payload.excerpt: A symbolic ceremony is a wedding ceremony with no legal effect. Here is what it means, how it differs from a legal wedding, and how Australian couples marry legally and still celebrate with a symbolic ceremony abroad.
key_takeaways: A symbolic ceremony carries no legal weight, so it can take any form, in any place, led by anyone you choose.
To marry legally in Australia you lodge a Notice of Intended Marriage at least 1 month and no more than 18 months ahead, and an authorised celebrant marries you in person.
Marrying legally overseas depends on the destination's own law, and the documents it asks for are set by that country.
A common route is a small legal ceremony in Australia and a symbolic ceremony at the destination for the celebration itself.

faq.q: Is a symbolic ceremony a real wedding?
faq.a: It is a real ceremony, with real vows and real guests, but it is not a legal marriage. The legal marriage happens separately, in Australia or under the destination's law.

faq.q: Is a symbolic ceremony legally binding in Australia?
faq.a: No. A legal marriage in Australia needs a [Notice of Intended Marriage, the specific words and an authorised marriage celebrant](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married), and a symbolic ceremony has none of these. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

faq.q: Can we marry legally in Australia and have a symbolic ceremony abroad?
faq.a: Yes. You give your Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant [at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the legal wedding](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married), hold a small legal ceremony in Australia, and celebrate abroad with a symbolic ceremony. Talk your dates through with your celebrant.

faq.q: Do we need a celebrant for a symbolic ceremony?
faq.a: No. Anyone you choose can lead it, in a symbolic role only.

faq.q: Can a friend lead our symbolic ceremony?
faq.a: Yes. A friend or family member can lead a symbolic ceremony. They cannot make it a legal marriage, so the legal ceremony still needs an authorised celebrant in Australia or the destination's own legal process.

faq.q: What is the difference between a symbolic ceremony and a vow renewal?
faq.a: A symbolic ceremony celebrates a marriage that is made legal separately. A vow renewal is for couples who are already married and want to say their vows again. See our [vow renewal ideas](/expert-advice/vow-renewal-ideas).

faq.q: Will our overseas marriage be recognised in Australia?
faq.a: An overseas marriage [cannot be registered in Australia, but it is generally recognised](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married) if it was a valid marriage in the overseas country and would have been a valid marriage here. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
